newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-INDIA TAKE CONTROL DESPITE LOSING THREE QUICK WICKETS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA TAKE CONTROL DESPITE LOSING THREE QUICK WICKETS.

text.p: South Africa collected three quick wickets in the afternoon session but India batted well enough to take control of the third and final test at the Wanderers on Sunday.
By tea on the fourth day the Indians had extended their first innings lead of 89 to 266 as they reached 177 for three in their second innings.

An opening partnership of 90 between Vikram Rathore and Nayan Mongia set the tone and, although South Africa fought back to take three wickets in seven overs, first innings century-maker Rahul Dravid and Saurav Ganguly cemented the touring team's position with a undefeated partnership of 53.

Mongia was the first to go, one ball after reaching 50. He got into a tangle against the pace of Allan Donald and edged a short ball to Brian McMillan at second slip. Mongia hit six fours from 89 deliveries.
Rathore fell four overs later, palpably lbw to Donald for a test best 44 from 111 balls with five fours.
South African captain Hansie Cronje then completed a notable double by removing his opposite number Sachin Tendulkar for the second time in the match, this time caught behind for nine.
Tendulkar fell with the Indian total on 124 for three but Dravid (31 not out) and Ganguly (37 not out) snuffed out any hopes South Africa may have harboured of dismissing India cheaply.
